newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore 1996 manufacturing investment up 19 pct.
newsitem.headline: Singapore 1996 manufacturing investment up 19 pct.

text.p: Singapore attracted Singapore S$8.1 billion in fixed asset investment commitments in manufacturing in 1996, a 19 percent increase over 1995, said the Economic Development Board (EDB) on Thursday.
It said in a statement Singapore was the biggest investor, followed by the United States and Japan.
It said the electronics sector made up 42.6 percent of the total investment. The chemicals sector invested 36.7 percent and manufacturing systems 8.2 percent.

The EDB saw higher fixed asset investments in the manufacturing sector in 1997 in line with an expected turnaround in the Singapore economy and improvement in the electronic sector. It expected several major projects to come on stream in 1997.
"There is intense competition for the investment dollar within the region and from developed countries," said the EDB statement.
To enhance competitiveness, EDB would work to build capabilities and promote innovation in industries and companies. It would examine pricing of resources like land and manpower.
